key_insight: Nearly uniform upward liquid flow in clean spherical bubble chains arises from the spatial arrangement of bubble far wakes, not just the chain’s overall dispersion width.
engineering_relevance: A reduced-order wake-superposition model can predict bubble-induced liquid flow from measured bubble trajectories, helping design and interpret gas–liquid flow systems.
method: High-accuracy embedded-boundary simulations resolved interfacial boundary layers and long-range bubble–bubble interactions.
Hydrodynamic interaction evolution was quantified to determine when isolated-bubble far wakes can be superposed.
A reduced-order model was built and tested against experimentally measured bubble trajectories and a uniformly dispersed reference case.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced the experimentally observed nearly uniform upward liquid flow, while the same-width uniformly dispersed arrangement produced a center-peaked velocity profile.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate bubble-trajectory information and may be less reliable when wake interactions, deformation, or non-clean interfaces violate the assumed far-wake superposition.
paper_title: Prediction of Spherical Bubble-Chain-Induced Liquid Flow through Far-Wake Superposition Based on Bubble-Chain Hydrodynamics
